newsitem.title: FRANCE: France against rushing 1998 EMU members decision.
newsitem.headline: France against rushing 1998 EMU members decision.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday that France was opposed to any rushing of the decision in early 1998 on which countries qualify to join monetary union at its launch in January 1999.
"France does not want any telescoping," he told a news conference.
Finance Ministry sources say they see the decision being made in late April or early May.
European Union finance ministers are due to discuss the timing of the decision at a meeting in Noordwijk, in the Netherlands, on Saturday.
France is keen to ensure that there is no overlap between the decision on membership of economic and monetary union (EMU) and its parliamentary elections, due in March 1998.
But French officials have also argued that practically it would be difficult to make the decision before April.

European Union leaders will decide which countries can join EMU at the start on the basis of actual economic and fiscal performance in 1997. Those figures are unlikely to be available before late February.
The European Commission and European Monetary Institute must then prepare recommendations about which countries they consider eligible to join the single currency in 1999.
